source_span: With the 10-year above 5%, bearish duration positioning close to historical extremes and inflation and credibility premia increasingly embedded in long-end yields, 25bp of tightening at the front end may now be the most bond-friendly outcome available to the Fed.
source_chain: 10-year already above 5% with DB's bond-positioning composite at the 5th percentile (near-record bearish) and credibility premium priced in, therefore a credible 25bp hike removes the upside-surprise risk that conventionally sells off bonds, therefore the hike becomes the bond-friendly outcome and can spark a tactical rally as one-sided shorts cover (amplified by CTA convexity) — invalidated by sustained trading above 5.15%-5.20% or the Fed endorsing a longer hiking cycle or the energy shock intensifying, confirmed by a retrace toward 4.73%-4.81%.
pulse_chain: The Fed delivered the most hawkish hike available into bond positioning already at the 5th percentile (near-record bearish), therefore there was almost nobody left to sell, therefore the hike's credibility removed the fear of the Fed being behind that had driven the selloff above 5%, therefore yields fell back to 4.95% and the short-$TLT call paid — resolved going forward by whether the 51%-priced October hike lands, deciding if the rally is bears closing out or a real turn.
why: The pulse keeps the note's mechanism (extreme short positioning plus a credible hike producing an unexpected bond rally) but swaps TME's falsifiable invalidation (a yield-level test at 5.15%-5.20% vs. a retrace to 4.73%-4.81%, or the Fed endorsing a longer cycle/energy shock intensifying) for an unrelated condition, the October FOMC's 51%-priced hike odds, which the source note never proposes as the test of its own thesis.
